plates.title: The Spine: From the Question to the Summa
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page, vellum-toned, with gold-leaf initials and vine-work borders, ten small bordered roundel scenes arranged in a single vertical column from top to bottom, connected by thin gilded cord-lines showing the flow of the argument (the fan nodes s1-s4 branching side by side from the recording-workshop roundel before converging into the toppling-tablets roundel). From top: a robed scholar beneath a glowing sun-brain (THE GRAND CHALLENGE); two bell-ringers in matched rhythm (TWO BELLS IN STEP); an ink river flowing scribe to scribe (THE RIVER OF FLOW); a mason chiselling a stone block into wedges, with FIGURE A redrawn in the manuscript's own linework as a small cartouche beside him showing the nested ovals of redundant/unique/synergistic information (CUTTING THE STONE); a workshop with a pinned brain-slice and tallying scribe (THE GRIDDED SLICE); then branching into four side-by-side roundels at the same height — a walled inner court of glowing figures (THE INNER COURT), two figures clasping hands in a loop (THE CLASPED LOOP), a banner on a modest mountain rise (THE MODEST SUMMIT), a monkey's reaching arm trailing scrolls (THE REACHING ARM) — all four cords rejoining into a clerk crushed under toppling tablets (THE TOPPLING TABLETS); ending at a weighing figure reading a coin's pattern instead of its count (READING THE PATTERN). Include a small cartouche near the fan-roundels redrawn in manuscript linework after FIGURE D, showing its branching result-panels as a cluster of small marked charts held by a figure comparing them. Palette: aged parchment cream, iron-gall brown ink, muted gold leaf, dusty blue and oxblood red accents. No lettering anywhere except the exact titles given, lettered in plain capitals beneath each roundel. Vignettes large and legible, filling the page width and height; margins bear only sparse vine-work, no crowding.

vignettes.quote: A grand challenge of modern neuroscience is to discover how brains “process information”
vignettes.depicts: A robed scholar at a lectern gazes up at a glowing brain suspended in the sky like a sun, quill poised over a blank page — the opening puzzle of the whole folio.
vignettes.title: THE GRAND CHALLENGE

vignettes.quote: It can be thought of as a nonlinear correlation between two patterns of activity
vignettes.depicts: Two small bell-ringers pulling ropes in matched rhythm, their two bells drawn touching in a shared halo of sound — likeness without direction.
vignettes.title: TWO BELLS IN STEP

vignettes.quote: Information transfer captures the overall “flow” of information through the system
vignettes.depicts: A river of ink flowing from one scribe's inkwell into a second scribe's page, but the second scribe's hand is shown frozen mid-stroke, unable to say what pattern the ink will form.
vignettes.title: THE RIVER OF FLOW

vignettes.quote: This parsing is accomplished using the partial information decomposition (PID) framework
vignettes.depicts: A master mason cutting a single stone block into labelled wedges with chisel and compass — the article's own nested-oval diagram rendered as FIGURE A set into a roundel beside him.
vignettes.title: CUTTING THE STONE

vignettes.quote: triads with more recurrent connections also had greater synergy
vignettes.depicts: Two source-figures holding hands in a closed loop while a third feedback-thread from the target above hangs slack and unused.
vignettes.title: THE CLASPED LOOP

vignettes.quote: the peak in synergy occurred when the mutual information was about 7% of the maximal value
vignettes.depicts: A mountain path with a bright banner planted at a modest rise partway up, while the summit beyond lies in shadow — synergy's single peak before the climb overshoots it.
vignettes.title: THE MODEST SUMMIT

vignettes.quote: during movement execution (a reach-and-grasp action) the relative abundance of redundant information increased dramatically
vignettes.depicts: A monkey's arm reaching to grasp a fruit, with many identical scrolls fluttering down the arm at once, each repeating the same instruction — duplicated signals for a safe grasp.
vignettes.title: THE REACHING ARM

plates.title: Inside: Cutting the Stone of Joint Information
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page continuing the same hand, vellum cream ground, iron-gall brown line, gold leaf accents, oxblood and dusty blue highlights. Seven roundels run top to bottom in a single reading column, connected by thin gilt cord. Top: a merchant with unbalanced scales, one large sack opposite several small sacks (THE UNBALANCED SCALES). Next: a hooded figure combining two ingredients in a mortar to make a glowing third (THE MORTAR AND PESTLE). Next: two masons unveiling finished stone wedges to onlookers (THE MASONS' UNVEILING). Next, the largest roundel on the page: FIGURE A redrawn in the manuscript's own linework — nested ovals, two overlapping source-circles within one outer oval, a reserved sliver standing for what neither circle covers alone (THE FOUR STONE WEDGES). Next: a clerk's ledger with three columns filled and one blank (THE UNFINISHED LEDGER). Next: a cartographer charting every cluster of three islands on a map, (CHARTING THE ISLANDS). Last, a second large roundel: FIGURE B redrawn as a branching trellis-lattice of linked wooden nodes climbing upward, a gardener's hand pruning them one at a time from the bottom rungs up (THE PRUNED TRELLIS). No lettering anywhere on the page except the given titles in plain capitals beneath each roundel. Vignettes large, filling the page's width, with only sparse vine-work in the margins — no crowding, no extra ornament.

plates.title: Inside: What the Decomposition Found
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page in the same hand as the prior plates: parchment cream ground, iron-gall brown ink, gold leaf, dusty blue and oxblood accents. Seven roundels run top to bottom joined by thin gilt cord, with a fork partway down the column (three roundels set side by side at the same height before rejoining). Top: the gridded brain-slice workshop opening the plate, repeated from the overview, pins and threads to a tallying scribe (THE GRIDDED SLICE REVISITED). Next: a miller filling one sack a quarter full from a larger sack, with FIGURE D's feedforward-versus-synergy scatter redrawn small in manuscript linework in a cartouche beside him (ONE SACK IN FOUR). Then the column forks into three roundels abreast: a bright walled court beside a plainer court, a scribe marking the difference (THE BRIGHTER COURT); two clasped figures glowing brighter than an unlinked pair beside them (THE DOUBLED CLASP); a small flag on a low mountain rise with a shadowed summit beyond (THE FLAG AT THE RISE). The three cords rejoin into a surveyor using one short rope yet marking too many boundary-posts around a field (THE OVER-EAGER SURVEYOR). Final roundel: a monkey's arm reaching to grasp a fruit, a dense flock of identical scrolls cascading down the limb (THE CASCADE OF SCROLLS). No lettering anywhere on the page except the given titles lettered in plain capitals beneath each roundel. Scenes large and clear, filling the page's width as well as its height; margins hold only sparse vine-work, never crowding the roundels.
